    23	Dear Mr. Roby:
    24	On various dates between August 2021 and October 2021, a representative of the Pipeline and
    25	Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Pipeline Safety (OPS), pursuant to
    26	Chapter 601 of 49 United States Code (U.S.C.), inspected Bayou Midstream’s subsidiary NST
    27	Transload Operating Company, LLC’s (NST) East Fairview, North Dakota pipeline terminal.
    28	As a result of the inspection, it is alleged that NST has committed probable violations of the Pipeline
    29	Safety Regulations, Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). The items inspected and the
    30	probable violations are:
    31	1.
    32	
    33	§195.452 Pipeline integrity management in high consequence areas.
    34	(a)….
    35	(b) What program and practices must operators use to manage pipeline integrity? Each
    36	operator of a pipeline covered by this section must:
    37	(1) Develop a written integrity management program that addresses the risks on each
    38	segment of pipeline.…
    39	(5) Implement and follow the program.
    40	NST failed to follow its integrity management procedure for risk analysis in Section 6 of the
    41	Northstar Midstream IMP to evaluate the consequences of a potential pipeline failure, as
    42	required by §195.452(f)(3). Specifically, NST failed to evaluate the consequences of a failure
    43	at its East Fairview terminal because it did not estimate the extent of dispersion of hazardous
    44	
    45	 materials that could result from a failure of the breakout tanks or piping. During the inspection
    46	NST could not provide records demonstrating that an analysis of a potential crude oil release
    47	had been conducted.
    48	2.
    49	
    50	§195.563 Which pipelines must have cathodic protection?
    51	(a) Each buried or submerged pipeline that is constructed, relocated, replaced, or
    52	otherwise changed after the applicable date in §195.401(c) must have cathodic protection.
    53	The cathodic protection must be in operation not later than 1 year after the pipeline is
    54	constructed, relocated, replaced, or otherwise changed, as applicable.
    55	NST failed to demonstrate that it had a functional cathodic protection (CP) system installed in
    56	its East Fairview station within one year of operation. During the inspection NST provided a
    57	map of the existing test points on its mainline pipe; however, there were no test points shown
    58	within the station. Additionally, PHMSA found from observation that electrical isolation kits
    59	had been installed between the mainline and station piping, indicating that the CP system in
    60	place for mainline pipe was not designed for the station piping.

60	place for mainline pipe was not designed for the station piping.
    61	The pipeline was fully operational in 2017, however NST failed to install a CP system within
    62	one year of operation and could not provide a justification for not installing CP; therefore, NST
    63	was operating without adequate CP.

    65	Proposed Compliance Order
    66	With respect to items 1, and 2, pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials
    67	Safety Administration proposes to issue a Compliance Order to NST Express LLC. Please refer to the
    68	Proposed Compliance Order, which is enclosed and made a part of this Notice.
    69	Response to this Notice
    70	Enclosed as part of this Notice is a document entitled Response Options for Pipeline Operators in
    71	Enforcement Proceedings. Please refer to this document and note the response options. All material
    72	you submit in response to this enforcement action may be made publicly available. If you believe that
    73	any portion of your responsive material qualifies for confidential treatment under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b),
    74	along with the complete original document you must provide a second copy of the document with the
    75	portions you believe qualify for confidential treatment redacted and an explanation of why you believe
    76	the redacted information qualifies for confidential treatment under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b).
    77	Following the receipt of this Notice, you have 30 days to submit written comments, or request a
    78	hearing under 49 CFR § 190.211. If you do not respond within 30 days of receipt of this Notice, this
    79	constitutes a waiver of your right to contest the allegations in this Notice and authorizes the Associate
    80	Administrator for Pipeline Safety to find facts as alleged in this Notice without further notice to you
    81	and to issue a Final Order. If you are responding to this Notice, we propose that you submit your
    82	correspondence to my office within 30 days from receipt of this Notice. This period may be extended
    83	by written request for good cause.
